2026-11-20.title: Friday of the Thirty-third Week in Ordinary Time
readings: I took the little scroll and ate it
How sweet to my taste is your promise!
My house shall be a house of prayer
2026-11-20.verse: It is written, ‘My house shall be a house of prayer’; but you have made it a den of robbers.
theo: John is told to take the little scroll and eat it: “it was sweet as honey in my mouth, but when I had eaten it, my stomach was made bitter.” Like Ezekiel before him, the prophet must first digest God's word before he can speak it. The word is sweet because it is God's; it is bitter because it carries judgement and suffering. Whoever proclaims it must first let it enter his own life.

Jesus enters the Temple and drives out the sellers, quoting Isaiah and Jeremiah: “My house shall be a house of prayer; but you have made it a den of robbers.” Then he teaches there daily, and the leaders cannot act against him, “for all the people were spellbound by what they heard”. The cleansed Temple becomes a school of the Word. Our churches and our hearts are meant to be the same: houses of prayer where God's word is heard and loved.
outline: Ask: how much of God's word did you “eat” this week?
God's word must be digested before it is proclaimed.
Cleanse what turns prayer into business.
“My house shall be a house of prayer.”
live: Read today's Gospel three times slowly and keep one phrase all day.
Set up or tidy a prayer corner at home.
2026-11-20.prayer: Lord, your words are sweeter than honey. Let me eat your word and let it change me, even when it is bitter. Cleanse my heart and make it a house of prayer. Amen.

quick: God's word must be digested before it is proclaimed.
The word is sweet, and sometimes bitter.
Our churches and hearts are houses of prayer.
2026-11-20.action: Tidy or set up a prayer corner at home.
2026-11-20.question: What turns my prayer into business?

homily: Dear friends, John is told to take the little scroll from the angel's hand and eat it. It was sweet as honey in his mouth, but when he had eaten it his stomach was made bitter (Revelation 10:9–10). Like Ezekiel before him, the prophet must first digest God's word before he can speak it.

The word is sweet because it is God's: it consoles, it heals, it gives hope. It is also bitter, because it calls us to conversion and carries the cost of the Cross. Whoever proclaims it, parent, catechist or priest, must first let it enter his own life.

In the Gospel Jesus enters the Temple and drives out those who were selling, saying: my house shall be a house of prayer, but you have made it a den of robbers. And every day he was teaching in the Temple, and all the people were spellbound by what they heard (Luke 19:46–48).

Our churches, our homes and our hearts are meant to be houses of prayer. Let us clear out what crowds God out, and let us eat his word: read the Sunday Gospel at home every Saturday evening, slowly, so that on Sunday it is already in us. Amen.
kids: Children, God's word is sweeter than honey! Ask your parents to read the Sunday Gospel with you on Saturday night.

intro: Eat God's word, delight in it, and keep God's house a house of prayer.

sub: Ezekiel and John ate the word.
It enters the prophet's life first.
Only then can he speak it.
q: He said to me, Mortal, eat this scroll that I give you and fill your stomach with it. Then I ate it; and in my mouth it was as sweet as honey.
So I took the little scroll from the hand of the angel and ate it; it was sweet as honey in my mouth, but when I had eaten it, my stomach was made bitter.
points.apply: Read today's Gospel three times slowly.

sub: The people hung on Jesus' words.
Love for Scripture grows with use.
q: How sweet are your words to my taste, sweeter than honey to my mouth!
But they did not find anything they could do, for all the people were spellbound by what they heard.
Has this house, which is called by my name, become a den of robbers in your sight? You know, I too am watching, says the LORD.
It is written, ‘My house shall be a house of prayer’; but you have made it a den of robbers.

concl: Eat the word, and it will make you a house of prayer.
Let Jesus teach daily in your temple.
